title: Deduplicate the Fast-Track-for-Simple-Tasks section between AGENTS.md and PROTOCOL.md, and make explicit that Simple Tasks skip the mandatory master-source read
objective: Owner is mid-refactor of the AI coordination system to reduce token overhead (already in flight: migrating .ai/state/tasks/*.json to .ai/state/tasks/<status>/*.json, and adding a Fast-Track protocol for Simple Tasks to both AGENTS.md and PROTOCOL.md). Direct research (git diff of both files) found the owner's own new Fast-Track section duplicated almost verbatim across both documents (~21 lines in AGENTS.md, ~24 in PROTOCOL.md, same criteria/workflow restated differently) -- exactly the kind of redundancy working against their stated goal. Owner confirmed via AskUserQuestion: consolidate so each file has one distinct job (AGENTS.md keeps the Simple-Task *definition*: criteria + examples; PROTOCOL.md keeps the Fast-Track *workflow mechanics*: conflict-check procedure, logging format, referencing AGENTS.md for the definition instead of restating it), and add an explicit line that Simple Tasks are exempt from the mandatory GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md/CURRENT_PLANNING_STATE.md read (AGENTS.md's 'Required reading' step) since that's the single largest token cost in the whole system and Simple Tasks are non-structural by definition. Two other findings from the same research pass (an incomplete .ai/state/tasks/<status>/ migration -- only 5 of ~113 files moved, a real conflict-detection gap; and verbose task-record objective/validations fields) were explicitly NOT chosen for this task -- out of scope here, flagged for a separate task. This task record itself is created directly under .ai/state/tasks/in_progress/ (the new status-subdirectory layout), one of the first non-ADR tasks to do so.
validations: DONE: consolidated the Fast-Track section so each file has one job -- AGENTS.md keeps the Simple-Task definition (criteria + examples) and now states explicitly that Simple Tasks are exempt from the mandatory GRAFTING_MASTER_SOURCE.md/CURRENT_PLANNING_STATE.md read; PROTOCOL.md keeps only the workflow mechanics (conflict check, validation, logging format) and points back to AGENTS.md for the definition instead of restating it. Net: ~45 duplicated lines across both files reduced to ~40 lines total with zero restated content.

DONE: ran this repository's own AI-state coordination validator (`uv run --package automation python -m automation.coordination --root .`) per PROTOCOL.md's own Validation section. It fails, but for a pre-existing reason unrelated to this task's own edits: a handoff record references task_id COORDINATION-PHASE1, whose task file still sits flat at .ai/state/tasks/COORDINATION-PHASE1.json (not yet moved into any status subdirectory) -- coordination.py's own new validate_repository only collects task_paths from status subdirectories, so it can't find that task_id and reports it as unknown. This is the same incomplete-migration gap flagged as finding #1 in the earlier audit (deliberately deferred, not this task's scope) surfacing as a concrete validator failure, not just a latent risk -- confirmed by inspection, not fixed here, since the owner explicitly chose this task (Fast-Track dedup) over finishing the migration this round.
artifacts: AGENTS.md (Fast-Track section trimmed to the Simple-Task definition + explicit master-source-read exemption)
.ai/coordination/PROTOCOL.md (Fast-Track section trimmed to workflow mechanics only)
risks: The repository's coordination validator (uv run --package automation python -m automation.coordination --root .) currently fails for a pre-existing, unrelated reason: the .ai/state/tasks/<status>/ migration the owner started is incomplete (~108 of ~113 task files still flat, not yet moved into a status subdirectory), and a handoff record references one of those flat tasks (COORDINATION-PHASE1) by task_id, which the new validator can no longer find. This was true before this task's edits and remains true after -- flagged here for visibility, not fixed, since the owner explicitly deferred finishing that migration to a separate task.
This task only proves the .md edits themselves are correct and non-duplicated -- none of this session's uncommitted changes have been committed or pushed yet.
